hero.body: A community-owned tourism ecosystem built with the Ê Đê people of Đắk Lắk, where every experience is authentic, every benefit is local, and every journey leaves something behind worth keeping.

items.title: Direct Economic Empowerment
items.body: A peer-to-peer marketplace that lets travelers book and buy directly from Ê Đê providers, so the value of an experience stays with the household that created it.

items.title: Cultural Preservation
items.body: An interactive digital archive of Ê Đê history, traditions, and language, developed in collaboration with community members and reviewed by elders.

items.title: Environmental Stewardship
items.body: A carbon footprint tracker that channels offset contributions into conservation projects run and measured by communities in the Central Highlands.

items.title: Community Engagement
items.body: Governance structures that give the Ê Đê community a direct voice in how the platform evolves and how revenue is distributed.

culture.body: The Ê Đê are one of the largest ethnic minority groups in the Central Highlands of Vietnam, with a matrilineal social structure that has governed community life for generations. Their culture is preserved in the rhythm of the Cồng Chiêng, the craft of their weavers, and the enduring architecture of the longhouse.

items.title: Cồng Chiêng — UNESCO Intangible Heritage
items.body: Recognised by UNESCO in 2005, the Cồng Chiêng tradition is not merely music. It is a language that connects the living with their ancestors, performed around the fire at every gathering of significance.

items.title: The Longhouse — Architecture of Community
items.body: The Knă is the architectural heart of Ê Đê life. Extended families live together under one roof, governed by a matriarch. It is the gathering place, the memory keeper, and the source of this platform's name.

items.title: Weaving and Craft — Stories in Thread
items.body: Ê Đê textile traditions encode identity and story in every pattern. Each piece is woven by hand using techniques passed down through generations, carrying a meaning that no reproduction can replicate.

transparency.heading: Tracked, not promised.
transparency.body: Every transaction on KNĂ is recorded on a public ledger. Travelers see where their money goes. Communities see what they earned. Partners verify what they claim.
transparency.quote: “Transparency stops being a slogan when anyone can check.”

community.body: Cultural content is reviewed by community elders. Service providers are verified by community representatives. Revenue distribution decisions sit with a council of Ê Đê stakeholders, not a corporate board. KNĂ exists in service of the longhouse it is named after.

invitation.body: The longhouse is wide. There is room for travelers who arrive in good faith.

footer.tagline: A responsible tourism platform for the Ê Đê people of Đắk Lắk. Built for the BKI 2026 competition by students of Ho Chi Minh City University of Economics and Finance.
footer.newsletterBody: Decisions and allocations are published on the community page as they happen.

review.title: Nothing is published until someone here says so.
review.intro: Submissions from households wait in this queue. Publishing puts an entry into the public archive; refusing keeps it with the household. Either way the reason is recorded, and a refusal cannot be filed without one.
review.notCommitteeTitle: This queue belongs to the Committee.
review.notCommitteeBody: Only members of the Community Governance Committee can review submissions. Seats are nominated by each buôn — they are not something the platform grants.
review.oldestFirst: Oldest first, so nothing waits forever.
review.reasonLabel: Reason — required to refuse, optional to publish
review.decidedBody: The full record, refusals included. This is what makes the archive auditable after the fact rather than only at the moment of publishing.

dashboard.noProviderBody: This page is for hosts, guides, and makers listing on KNĂ. Becoming a provider means being verified by a community representative in your buôn.
dashboard.queueIntro: Check the dates with the household, then confirm here. Declining releases the booking and removes it from the public ledger.
dashboard.queueEmpty: Nothing waiting. Every booking has been decided.

dashboard.earningsNote: Bookings still awaiting confirmation are not counted as earnings — nobody has agreed the dates yet. Every figure here also appears on the public ledger.

explore.title: A record kept by the people it belongs to.
explore.intro: Every recording, story, and photograph here was contributed by an Ê Đê household and reviewed by the Community Governance Committee before publication. Nothing is uploaded about the community without the community.
explore.pillarsHeading: Three traditions carry most of what the Ê Đê know about themselves.

pillars.body: A gong is not an instrument here. It is a voice. Each set is tuned to a family, played at births, harvests, and funerals, and read by listeners the way a letter is read.
A house grows with its family. New sections are added as daughters marry, so the length of a longhouse records how many generations have lived under it.
Motifs are not ornament. They mark clan, region, and the occasion a cloth was made for. A weaver reading another weaver’s work can name the village it came from.

explore.browseHeading: Everything, indexed by the household that shared it.
explore.emptyCategory: Nothing published in that category yet.
explore.mediaPendingBody: Entry records are live and moderated. The audio, 360° tours, and photo essays themselves are not hosted yet — media storage is the next piece of this screen.
explore.phrasesHeading: {{count}} phrases change how you are received.
explore.phrasesBody: The Ê Đê language is spoken daily in the buôn but rarely by visitors. Learning even a greeting signals that you came to meet people rather than to look at them.
explore.phrasesScope: Everyday speech is published by decision of the Committee, April 2026. Ceremonial and clan-specific speech is not, and will not appear here.
explore.phrasesAudio: Pronunciation audio is recorded but not yet hosted.
explore.handoffBody: Every household in this archive also hosts, guides, or sells through KNĂ.

travel.title: Every listing is somebody’s home, work, or calendar.
travel.intro: Ê Đê households set their own prices, their own dates, and their own house rules. KNĂ verifies them, carries the booking, and shows you what reaches them.
travel.verifiedBody: A community representative has visited the household, confirmed the person listing is the person hosting, and checked that the cultural content described is theirs to share. Verification is renewed each season.
travel.searchPlaceholder: Search a host, a buôn, or a craft
travel.emptyBody: Only four buôn have onboarded so far. Try a wider filter.
travel.bookingError: Could not send that booking. Try again.
travel.splitHeading: The split is written into the contract, not the marketing.
travel.splitBody: Every booking is computed the same way on the server and written to the public ledger the moment you book — see it on the Community page.

split.note: Paid directly to the household or co-op that hosts you.
Heritage work and conservation, allocated by the Community Governance Committee.
Runs the platform, verification, and provider training.

travel.splitNote: Marketplace purchases use a different split: artisans keep 95%.
travel.handoffBody: The same households sell their work through the marketplace, with the same verification.

marketplace.title: Made by a person you can name.
marketplace.intro: Artisans set their own prices and keep 95% of what you pay — verified by the same community representatives who verify hosts and guides.
marketplace.certHeading: Authenticity you’ll be able to check, not a label you have to trust.
marketplace.certBody: The plan: register each piece when the maker finishes it, so scanning a tag opens the same record — who made it, where, how long it took — alongside the payment that reached the household. Every order today is still verified by the Community Governance Committee; the scannable certificate itself is on the roadmap.
marketplace.certNote: Certificates will be issued by the Community Governance Committee, not by KNĂ. Only work made by a registered Ê Đê household will be able to carry one.
marketplace.searchPlaceholder: Search a maker, a material, or a piece
marketplace.emptyTitle: No pieces in that category yet.
marketplace.emptyBody: Makers list when a piece is finished, so stock moves slowly by design.
marketplace.orderError: Could not place that order. Try again.
marketplace.notesHeading: Handmade means slow, and sometimes means no.

notes.b: If a listing says one, there is one. Nothing here is reproduced to meet demand, and a maker may decline a repeat commission.
Pieces ship from Đắk Lắk once a week. Allow two to three weeks within Vietnam, longer internationally.

notes.h: Some work is not for sale
notes.b: Certain ceremonial pieces are recorded in the cultural archive but never listed. The Committee decides what stays in the buôn.
KNĂ does not discount, run sales, or negotiate on a maker’s behalf. What you see is what they asked for.

marketplace.handoffHeading: Not sure what you are looking at?
marketplace.handoffBody: The assistant can explain a motif, a technique, or what a piece is traditionally for.

community.title: The decisions are made here, in the open.
community.intro: Representatives from the onboarded buôn govern what is published, what the Community Fund pays for, and who may list on the platform. Minutes and allocations are public, including the decisions that went against the platform.
community.statMeetings: meetings, minutes published within a week
community.committeeHeading: Named people, not a board of advisors.
community.committeeBody: Members are nominated by their own buôn and serve one-year terms. KNĂ attends meetings to answer questions and has no vote.
community.fundHeading: Three percent of every booking, spent line by line.
community.fundBody: The Fund is a pass-through, not platform revenue. The Committee decides what it pays for and publishes the allocation each quarter.
community.minutesHeading: Including the ones that said no.
community.minutesBody: A governance record that only contains approvals is not a governance record. Refusals are published with the same detail as decisions that passed.
community.boardBody: Planned to be readable by anyone, with posting limited to verified providers and Committee members.
community.boardNotBuiltBody: The board is on the roadmap and nobody has posted to it. The cards below are examples of what hosts told us they would use it for.

threads.author: A guide
threads.title: Forest walk moving to earlier starts from June
threads.body: The heat after ten is too much for guests and for me. Walks will start at six thirty from 1 June until the rains. Please update your listings if you run the same route.

threads.author: A weaver
threads.title: Indigo supply is short this season
threads.body: The dye plot flooded in April. I have enough for maybe four more pieces. If anyone in Trấp has surplus leaf I will trade rattan for it.

threads.author: A host
threads.title: Guests keep asking to help with cooking
threads.body: Is anyone else finding this? I do not mind but the kitchen is small. Wondering whether we should add it as a listed activity rather than let it happen by accident.

community.feedbackHeading: Your feedback goes to the Committee, not to a ratings algorithm.
community.feedbackBody: There are no star ratings on KNĂ. Comments are read at the monthly meeting and, where they concern a host, shared with that household first.

feedbackNotes.b: A four out of five on a family home is a judgement on a household, published permanently. Written comments carry the same information without that cost.
It goes to the host and to the Committee together. Serious or repeated issues can suspend a listing, and that decision appears in the minutes.

community.closingHeading: That is the whole of it.
community.closingBody: The archive, the experiences, the marketplace, the ledger, and the people who decide.

assistant.title: Ask the awkward questions here, not at the door.
assistant.intro: Most visitors cause offence by accident, because nobody told them. The assistant is trained on the community archive and will tell you plainly what is expected.
assistant.prototypeNote: This is a prototype. Answers come from a fixed script for now, and the four suggested questions are the ones wired up.
opening: I'm the KNĂ assistant. I can help you plan a route, explain what you'll see, or tell you how to behave somewhere so you don't cause offence without meaning to.
What I say about Ê Đê custom comes from the community archive, reviewed by elders. If I have not been told something, I will say so rather than guess.

prompts.label: How do I greet an elder?
prompts.reply:
Let the elder speak first. A short reply and a slight bow of the head is enough — Ê Đê greeting is not effusive, and a long enthusiastic introduction can read as pushy.

If you want a phrase, “Hê drei” works at any hour. “Bơni” is thank you.

One thing visitors often get wrong: in a matrilineal household the eldest woman is usually the person to address, even when a man greets you at the ladder.

prompts.label: What can I photograph?
prompts.reply:
Most of daily life is fine to photograph if you ask first. Three things to avoid:

• The ancestor shelf inside a longhouse. Not photographed, generally not discussed with visitors either.
• Funeral gongs or a funeral in progress.
• Children, without a parent present.

Ceremonies vary by household. If you booked through KNĂ, the house rule on your booking card tells you what that particular family has agreed to.

prompts.label: Plan me three days
prompts.reply:
Here is a shape that works for a first visit, low travel, one buôn per day:

Day 1 — Arrive Buôn Ma Thuột, afternoon at Buôn Akô Dhông. Short walk, meet your host, eat with the household. Stay the night.

Day 2 — Morning loom session with Amí Lan in Buôn Kli A. Afternoon free. Evening gong ensemble in Buôn Đôn if the harvest calendar has a date open.

Day 3 — Forest edge walk with Y Wik, then the coffee co-op in the afternoon. Depart evening.

Want me to check which dates actually have availability?

prompts.label: What is Cồng Chiêng?
prompts.reply:
A set of tuned gongs, and the practice around them. UNESCO recognised the Space of Gong Culture in the Central Highlands in 2005.

What matters more than the recognition: the gongs are not performed for an audience in the ordinary sense. A set is tuned to a family and played at births, harvests, and funerals. Listeners in the buôn can hear which occasion is being marked.

That is why KNĂ lists ceremony evenings only when the village is holding one anyway, rather than scheduling them for visitors.

assistant.fallback:
I don't have that in the community archive yet, so I'd rather not guess.

Your host is the better person to ask, and asking is usually welcome. If it's something the community thinks visitors should know, it can be submitted to the Governance Committee for the archive.
assistant.fallbackNote: Anything else you type will get the assistant’s “I don’t know” answer, which is deliberate. Try it.
assistant.inputPlaceholder: Ask about custom, a place, or your trip
assistant.guardrailsHeading: An assistant that speaks about a culture needs limits.

guardrails.b: Cultural answers come from the reviewed archive. Outside it, the assistant says so rather than filling the gap.

guardrails.h: It never speaks for a household
guardrails.b: House rules differ. The assistant points you to your host or your booking card instead of generalising.
Recommendations follow what you asked for and what is available, not what earns the platform more.
Elders and the Governance Committee can flag an answer. Corrections go into the archive, not into a private model.

assistant.handoffHeading: Ready to work out your footprint?
assistant.handoffBody: The assistant can estimate it, or you can do it yourself in the impact tracker.

carbon.title: Getting here has a cost. Here is the number.
carbon.intro: Most of a trip’s footprint is the journey, not the stay. The tracker shows the whole of it, then routes an offset to a project the community actually runs.
carbon.communityLedBody: Projects are identified by the buôn, approved by the Community Governance Committee, and reported on by the households doing the work.
carbon.noOverland: Overland options are not offered for this origin.
carbon.estimateNote: An estimate, not a measurement. Figures are indicative and will be replaced with a verified dataset before the platform goes live.
carbon.projectsHeading: Three projects, all within an hour of where you will be staying.
carbon.projectsBody: Choose one and the contribution is routed to that project’s account, not to a general fund. On two of the three you can join the work yourself at the end of your stay.

projects.name: Yok Đôn buffer replanting
projects.unit: native saplings, tended for three years
projects.body: Degraded buffer land on the park edge, replanted with dipterocarp and tended by the households that farm beside it. Survival is counted annually, not at planting.

projects.name: Lắk Lake watershed planting
projects.unit: bamboo and hardwood along the shoreline
projects.body: Shoreline planting to slow erosion into the lake. Run in the wet season, when saplings take without irrigation.

projects.name: Elephant corridor upkeep
projects.body: Supports the shift away from elephant riding by funding habitat and fodder for observation-based tourism instead.

carbon.joinableYes: You are invited to plant on the final day of your stay.
carbon.joinableNo: This project is maintained year-round by the conservation group.
carbon.afterwardsHeading: An offset you can follow, the same as any other payment.
carbon.afterwardsBody: Offset contributions sit on the same public ledger as bookings and purchases. You can see what was received and by whom.
carbon.afterwardsNote: Survival counts are published each year by the households running the site. A planting that fails is recorded as a failure.
carbon.handoffHeading: Who decides which projects get funded?
carbon.handoffBody: The Community Governance Committee. Their minutes, decisions, and fund allocations are published in the community space.
